name: Nepos Assertion Ontology
description: A formal model in which every biographical claim of the edition is an Assertion: a reified statement linking who asserted it (assertedBy), in which document (assertedIn), about what topic (hasTopic), grounded in which passage of the text (hasSourcePassage), with an explicit confidence value. Adapted from the Laertius assertion model.

classes.label: Assertion
classes.description: A reified biographical claim. Not a fact about the world, but a statement made by a source, which the edition records together with its provenance and confidence.

attributes.name: assertedBy
attributes.description: The person making the claim (here: Cornelius Nepos)

attributes.name: assertedIn
attributes.description: The document in which the claim is made

attributes.name: hasTopic
attributes.description: What kind of claim this is (birth, residence, travel, death, relationship...)

attributes.name: hasSourcePassage
attributes.description: The exact passage of the text that grounds the claim

attributes.name: reportsAssertion
attributes.description: When Nepos reports what others say (ferunt, dicitur), the inner assertion

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.description: How directly the text supports the claim

classes.label: Commander
classes.description: A subject of one of the Vitae, dux memoria dignus.

classes.label: NonCommander
classes.description: Any other person appearing in the text (fathers, kings, rivals, the author himself).

classes.label: Polity
classes.description: A state or people a commander served: Athens, Sparta, Thebes, Carthage, Persia, Rome.

classes.label: Place
classes.description: A geographic location that can be mapped.

classes.label: Topic
classes.description: A flat class: no hierarchy. The kinds of claims the edition tracks.

instances.label: Residence
instances.description: Where a person lived or was based

instances.label: Travel
instances.description: Where a person campaigned, fled, or journeyed

instances.label: Contemporary Of
instances.description: Person-to-person relations between contemporaries: colleagues, rivals, patrons, opponents

conventions: subtype: a concept branches into its kinds
Topic is a flat class: no hierarchy.
